# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 50/100, Needs work Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 11.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. High = (11.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. Every rule could be decided from the code, so the score is a single number. The main issues are that pages are built only in the browser, the Trail guides page is told to stay out of search, and the home page reaches that page only through a button. No blocker cap applied. The only page marked noindex everywhere is `/admin`, which looks deliberate. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Send real page content in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends and don't run JavaScript. With server rendering off, they may see an empty page. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line or set `ssr: true`, or prerender the routes. - **Score after this:** 63 (GEO-003 earns 3 of 3). ### 2. Remove the noindex header from `/guides` - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap, but this middleware tells search engines not to index it. That sends mixed signals, and your main content page is hidden. - **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` - **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` - **Size:** Small. Delete this middleware, or intentionally drop `/guides` from the sitemap if the noindex is wanted. - **Score after this:** 57 (GEO-014 earns 3 of 3 instead of 1.5). ### 3. Link to the guides with a real link - **Why it matters:** crawlers follow `` links. A button that calls a script gives them no address to follow, so `/guides` may never be found from the home page. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Use `Trail guides`. - **Score after this:** 59 (GEO-016 earns 2 of 2). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, plain text, valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says they should | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks only `/admin` for `*`. No config, so I assumed you want to be found | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/guides` noindex via `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`; `/` clear (1 of 2 routes) | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own domain | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:4-7`: head sets no canonical link, so `/` and `/guides` have none (0 of 2) | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, `ssr: false`, site-wide | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the project | | GEO-011 | Valid sitemap that is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4`: `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` is relative, and sitemap lines must be absolute | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` give every page the same title and description. `/` is fine, `/guides` is not (1 of 2). `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5` | | GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`: button with `router.push` (0 of 1 routes) | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts` sets only `noindex`. No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Not run | Read `app.vue`, `pages/index.vue`, `pages/guides.vue`. No images, the button has text, and a title is set | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | Not run | None present | ## Other problems found - **Sitemap lists a noindexed page:** `public/sitemap.xml:4`: `https://trailhead.example/guides`. The middleware at `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` marks it noindex. Fix: remove the header (item 2). - **Placeholder domain:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://trailhead.example/`. No real site origin is declared anywhere, so canonicals and the `Sitemap:` line can't point to a real domain. Fix: decide the real domain and use it in all three places. ## Worth considering - **The Trail guides page promises routes it doesn't list:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. Nothing is graded or listed. Listing each route as text, ideally each on its own page and address, might help readers and machines. - **The home page says little about the site:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. A short text description of the walks, with links to individual guides, might help visitors and crawlers see what the site covers. - **Each page needs its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });`. Set a distinct one with `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` on `/guides` and any new pages. - **Blocking `/admin` in robots.txt hides its noindex:** `pages/admin.vue:2` has `noindex` and `public/robots.txt:2` has `Disallow: /admin`. Crawlers blocked by robots.txt can't read the noindex. If the page is only private, this is fine as it is. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **GEO-014 header:** I counted the middleware header as a Problem because it's in the repository. If the site is hosted as static files with no Nitro server, it wouldn't run, so a live check would confirm what actually gets served. - **Sitemap URLs:** whether the listed URLs answer 200 needs a live check. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. - `/admin` is deliberately private, so I treated its noindex and robots block as intended and left it out of the route counts. - The middleware runs in production. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
